title: The chart generator remains regular after a coordinate quotient
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] with regular parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_d$, let $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}$ be nonempty, let $j\in J$, and let $A_j=R[u_i\mid i\in J\setminus\{j\}]/(t_i-t_j u_i)$ be the chart ring. Then multiplication by $t_j$ is injective on $A_j/(u_i)$ for every $i\in J\setminus\{j\}$ and on $A_j/(t_k)$ for every $k\notin J$.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 4.2.9 coordinate-chart computation, printed p. 121; algebraic nonzerodivisor check from Stacks Tag 0BIQ

proof.text: Fix one $i\in J\setminus\{j\}$ and put $H=J\setminus\{j,i\}$ and $B=R/(t_i)$; bars denote images in $B$. Setting only $u_i$ equal to zero in the defining presentation makes the relation $t_i-t_j u_i$ become $t_i=0$, and leaves every $u_h$ for $h\in H$ untouched. Thus, by the quotient universal property, $$A_j/(u_i)\cong B[u_h\mid h\in H]/(\bar t_h-\bar t_j u_h\mid h\in H).$$ Explicitly, the isomorphism sends each coefficient $r$ to its class $\bar r$ and each surviving variable $u_h$ to the same variable; the reverse assignment is well-defined because $t_i=t_j u_i=0$ in $A_j/(u_i)$. Order the original parameters with $t_i$ first, $t_j$ next, the $t_h$ for $h\in H$ next, and the remaining parameters last. The regular-parameter lemma gives a regular sequence in this order. By the definition of regular sequence its tail over $B$ is regular, and so is the initial segment $(\bar t_j,(\bar t_h)_{h\in H})$ of that tail. For $I_i=(\bar t_j,\bar t_h\mid h\in H)\subset B$, the chart-presentation lemma identifies the displayed quotient with $B[I_i/\bar t_j]$, taking $u_h$ to $\bar t_h/\bar t_j$ and the image of $t_j$ to the chart generator. Since $\bar t_j\in I_i$, the chart-generator lemma gives injectivity of multiplication by $t_j$ on this individual quotient. This proves the assertion for every such $i$; if $J=\{j\}$ there is no $i$ and the assertion is vacuous.

proof.text: Let $k\notin J$ and put $B=R/(t_k)$, with bars denoting images in $B$. Taking the quotient of the displayed presentation by $t_k$ gives $$A_j/(t_k)\cong B[u_h\mid h\in J\setminus\{j\}]/(\bar t_h-\bar t_j u_h\mid h\in J\setminus\{j\}).$$ The coefficient and variable maps in the two directions give this identification directly. Order the original parameters with $t_k$ first, then $t_j$, then the other $t_h$ for $h\in J$, and finally the remaining parameters. The regular-parameter lemma makes this a regular sequence. Hence, by the definition of regular sequence, the tail over $B$ is regular and so is its initial segment $(\bar t_j,(\bar t_h)_{h\in J\setminus\{j\}})$. Put $I_k=(\bar t_h:h\in J)\subset B$. The chart-presentation lemma identifies the displayed quotient with $B[I_k/\bar t_j]$, sending $u_h$ to $\bar t_h/\bar t_j$. Since $\bar t_j\in I_k$, the chart-generator lemma gives injectivity of multiplication by $\bar t_j$ on this algebra, which corresponds to multiplication by $t_j$ on $A_j/(t_k)$. When $J=\{j\}$ the polynomial variable set is empty and the chart is $B[(\bar t_j)/\bar t_j]=B$, with injectivity also given by regularity of the sequence $(t_k,t_j)$.

lean.statement: theorem traceChartCoordinateNonzerodivisors {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsRegularLocalRing R] {d : ℕ} (t : Fin d → R) (ht : IsLocalRing.IsRegularSystemOfParameters (List.ofFn t)) (J : Finset (Fin d)) (hJ : J.Nonempty) (j : Fin d) (hj : j ∈ J) : (∀ (i : Fin d) (hi : i ∈ J.erase j), Function.Injective (fun x : traceChartCoordinateQuotient t J j i hi => Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (algebraMap R (traceChartRing t J j) (t j)) * x)) ∧ (∀ k : Fin d, k ∉ J → Function.Injective (fun x : traceChartParameterQuotient t J j k => Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (algebraMap R (traceChartRing t J j) (t j)) * x))
